title: Tips to combat shoulder pain
summary: General overview of how to avoid and manage shoulder pain from benching, based on his own history of repeated right-shoulder injuries. He argues frequent flat barbell benching inevitably harms the shoulder, and recommends arching, bench variations, balancing with vertical pressing and lots of back work, careful shoulder isolation, dropping painful movements, band dislocates, and soft-tissue work.

claims.claim: Shoulder injuries are among the most common lifting injuries, ranking after lower back injuries and just before knee injuries.
Shoulder injuries are among the easiest to avoid, but a severe one often does not heal by itself and can require surgery; most cases are tweaks or tendonitis.
In four years of benching he injured himself several times: once a pec strain, otherwise always his right shoulder (rotator cuff sprains or AC joint issues).
The typical bench overuse sign is an achy soreness felt inside, between the pec and the shoulder, the day after benching.

He kept re-injuring his shoulder at the same point, around 285-295 lbs touch-and-go for 5-6 reps, rebuilding then getting hurt again, until at 23 he realized the problem was becoming chronic and changed his approach.
A year and a half after changing his approach he was pain-free and benching much more total volume than before.
High-frequency flat benching will damage your shoulders: horizontal presses are detrimental to shoulder health regardless of form, arch or scapular retraction.
Programs that have you bench raw three to five times a week are awful because they lead to rotator cuff lesions and shoulder impingement.

On any lying horizontal press, don't keep your back flat: the flatter the back, the further the bar travels and the deeper the shoulder dives into extension, straining it. Arch and keep shoulders back and tight to shorten the range.

Accept that you cannot bench raw all the time; use variations that deload the shoulder (reverse grip, close grip, slingshot, floor press, any dumbbell press) so the shoulder rests between flat barbell sessions.
Balance horizontal pressing with an equal amount of vertical pressing; full-range vertical presses are healthy for the shoulder.
Heavy dumbbell presses done with a short, partial range are not real vertical pressing and are bad for the shoulders.

Do overhead press for volume with a weight you can move at least 5 times through full range, finishing with the shoulder locked overhead, head through the window and thoracic extension held (elbow lockout optional).
He always finishes his horizontal pressing days with a vertical press, usually with a barbell.
Training back, lats, traps and rear delts keeps shoulders healthy by keeping the shoulders back and low and letting you stay tight when pressing; you should do more upper back work than pressing.
Pull-ups, especially through full range of motion, are excellent for shoulder health.
Shoulder isolation work (side raises, front raises, skull crushers) can increase shoulder pain; side raises done with internally rotated arms are 'shoulder impingement 101'.
Front raises are contentious; he agrees most people can drop them since front delts get enough work, but he does them heavy because he has never had issues with them.
If a movement hurts, stop doing it; you can return later with lower weight and fixed form.
If benching hurts but push-ups don't, replace most bench volume with push-ups and slowly rebuild the bench.
Do shoulder dislocates with a band, not a rigid bar; dislocates and pole/bar shoulder work are great for shoulder health.
Ice helps knee pain but for him rarely reaches the rotator cuff or AC joint through the muscle; it is the least important tip.
Rolling a lacrosse or medicine ball between shoulder and pec, and rolling the pec itself, can help since shoulder pain is sometimes linked to pec tightness.
Some lifters can bench with high frequency without shoulder pain, but they are outliers.
Any lift can be damaging if done too often, but overuse injuries are much more prevalent on the flat bench because of the shoulder's structure.
Skull crushers are not shoulder builders, but some people find the shoulder flexion needed to work the triceps long head painful.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
cues: shoulders back and tight in the pocket
exercises.why: shorter bar path means less shoulder extension and strain

exercises.name: Bench variations (reverse grip, close grip, slingshot, floor press, dumbbell press)
exercises.why: deload the shoulder so you can bench flat barbell more effectively

exercises.name: Overhead press
cues: weight you can do 5+ reps full range
lock shoulder overhead, head through the window
exercises.why: vertical pressing balances horizontal pressing and is healthy for the shoulder

exercises.name: Side raises
cues: feel medial and rear delts more than front

exercises.name: Front raises
exercises.why: optional; front delts get enough work, he does them heavy without issues

exercises.name: Push-ups
exercises.why: pain-free substitute for bench volume while rebuilding

exercises.name: Band shoulder dislocates
cues: use a band, not a rigid bar

exercises.name: Lacrosse ball rolling between pec and shoulder
cues: roll the pec to work out knots
exercises.why: shoulder pain can come from pec tightness
